what: Measured boundaries of record count-plateaus and of their extension regions.
IMPORTANT: Every boundary is a BRACKET between two sampled parameter values, never an exact locus. The true boundary is a wall (an algebraic condition) and has not been solved for. Quoting a bracket endpoint as the boundary would be wrong.

regions.parameterisation: q(t) = reduce((12-t)*A + t*B), integer, appended to eight fixed cubes
regions.A_note: the ORIGINAL n=9 representative; B is the simplified (109,-11,91,140) scaled by 814

increment.note: outside the count plateau the n=10 count tracks n=9 + 1138 exactly

bracket_history.method: simplest-rational (Stern-Brocot) bisection, not midpoint: a denominator q costs quaternion height ~q*1e5 on this line, so midpoint bisection prices itself out immediately. Cost of the representative is a free choice; the object is not.
bracket_history.engine: cube_regions_q2w. cube_regions_n returns 'degenerate plane triple' at several of these points -- an engine refusal, NOT a budget limit and NOT a negative. An earlier pass recorded t=13/3 as budget-stopped; the wide engine counts it 3925, which MOVED the bracket. 'Unevaluable is not a negative result.'
bracket_history.still_a_bracket: The wall is an algebraic number. 1/96 is 288x tighter, not exact. Closing it needs the wall POLYNOMIAL: identify which coincidence goes tight across this window and solve it. That is the remaining step.

regions.finding: walls are per-PAIR; the high-scoring extensions are the sensitive ones

count_plateau_dimensions.method: arc_eps.tangents_eps -- tangent candidates SOLVED from wall normals, each verified with eps in both signs, then combinations tested to separate a surface from a node. Controls on every row: zero displacement must reproduce the record, a wall-normal displacement must not. Both passed everywhere.
count_plateau_dimensions.why_not_probing: Three integer probes failed first. FAILURE_MODES 11d: a zero probe reading means 'not aligned', never 'isolated'; and a probe moving ONE cube cannot see a locus that is positive-dimensional only via multi-cube directions. A 1-dimensional plateau in a 3-dimensional tangent space is almost never axis-aligned. See P287 and the two postscripts after it.

n4_183.verdict: count plateau 0-dimensional -- third independent confirmation of P287

n6_727.verdict: 2 tangents; dim2785.log shows no combination holds -> NODE, two arcs crossing, not a surface. This row is the CONTROL: it reproduces a known result independently, which is what licenses the others.

count_plateau_dimensions.note_dimension_is_not_monotone: n=5 has a 0-dimensional count plateau while n=6 has arcs and n=9 has a plateau walked across t in [0,24]. Shape is a property of the particular record, not of the level.
count_plateau_dimensions.no_trend: tangent counts across the tower are 0, 0, 2, 1 at n = 4,5,6,7 -- not monotone. 727 is the outlier, not the start of a progression. Shape is a property of the particular record, not of the level.
count_plateau_dimensions.SCOPE_CORRECTION_2026_09_09: every tangent count in this file is LAST-CUBE-ONLY -- tangents_eps searches the last cube's slice by construction. Probing base directions shows the plateau is >=2-dimensional at n=7 (base direction = the arc D lift, not axis-aligned) and at n=8 (base direction = +-e15, which is n=7's surviving direction lifted). n=4,5,6 are UNRESOLVED, not zero: only axis directions were probed. See P297.

wall_data.what: distinct wall gradients per record, exported from dimension_cache
wall_data.cross_check: these counts reproduce tangents_eps's independently-reported wall counts exactly
wall_data.NOT_polynomials: wall GRADIENTS are linearisations at the record point, not the conditions' polynomials. Superseded 2026-09-08 by data/wall_keys.json, which records the reconstruction KEY -- see wall_keys below. This field is kept because the gradients are still the right object for a tangent test.
wall_data.why_it_was_missing: the runs computed walls (880s at n=6, 1498s at n=7) and reported only summary counts, discarding them. dimension.cached_conditions caches the expensive step, so recovery was cheap -- but nothing had ever written them out in a usable form.

wall_keys.what: the RECONSTRUCTION KEY for every distinct wall at every named record: (frame, group, sig, c0) plus the record quaternions. That tuple is the complete argument list of dimension.branch_numerator, which returns the exact polynomial P with f = 1 <=> P = 0. The key IS the polynomial.
wall_keys.n4_183: UNEVALUABLE, not skipped: cube 1 is a half-turn, the record is at Cayley infinity and this chart has no point for it (P287).

how_to_use.polynomial: import wall_keys as W; W.numerator(key, W.cvecs_of(quats))
how_to_use.on_a_cayley_line: W.on_line(key, q0, pt, dir) -> exact coefficients in t, low degree first
how_to_use.on_a_quaternion_line: W.on_quat_line(key, quats, moving, A, B, span) -> same, for q(t) = (span-t)A + tB. THIS is the form the project's brackets take (solve_wall.py); a quaternion line is a Moebius curve in Cayley coordinates, not a line, so on_line does not apply to it.

gates.G1: P(record) == 0 -- a wall contains its own point. Absolute anchor, outside the code.
gates.G2: dP/dt|0 == s*(grad.d) with ONE scale s across independent directions; grad comes from sympy diff of f, P from the numerator formula -- two routes.
gates.G3: negative control: corrupt the key (flip a sign in sig); G1 must then FAIL.
gates.gate_mn: quaternion route vs Cayley route along a Cayley line, compared as coefficient VECTORS up to proportionality (a hypersurface is defined up to scale).
gates.result: after the P288 fix: 12/18/27/51/75/20 walls, G1 all vanish, G2 all pass, G3 catches all. gate_mn 12/12 at n=4.

wall_keys.IMPORTANT: a key is complete ONLY together with the record quaternions stored beside it: the same key at another configuration is a different polynomial.
wall_keys.found_a_bug: G1 failed on 6/27 at n=6, 24/51 at n=7, 42/75 at n=8 before the fix, and EVERY failure had two distinct cubes in its group. See LEDGER P288 and FAILURE_MODES 32.
